key_insight: tEHR uses pretrained language semantics to model structured patient histories, with meaningful clinical descriptions and two-stage adaptation contributing to prediction performance.
clinical_relevance: This approach could support EHR-based risk prediction by leveraging the meanings of clinical events rather than treating them only as dataset-specific tokens.
method: Represent longitudinal EHR events using natural-language descriptions and numerical values.
Continue pretraining a causal language model on EHR text streams.
Apply task-specific discriminative fine-tuning with LoRA to predict outcomes.
evidence_signal: Evaluation covered four MIMIC-IV prediction tasks and CPRD pancreatic cancer prediction at 1–12-month horizons; the Mistral-7B-v0.3 backbone performed strongest overall.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish prospective clinical utility or generalizability beyond the evaluated datasets.
paper_title: Evaluating Pretrained Language Semantics for Structured EHR Prediction Tasks
